text:
Ben (Support): FYI customer reported websocket stream drops during long-running responses (~40-50s). They see a 100-continue then silence, client gets ECONNRESET. customer says this only happens from their corporate network (VPC + egress allowlist).
Alice (SRE): Can you paste the short reproducible steps and any connection id/trace id? Also whether they're behind any customer proxy / SEC appliance.
Ben (Support): Repro steps from customer: 1) Connect via wss to private endpoint through their VPC egress NAT 2) Send streaming request that yields ~60s of tokens 3) After ~45s stream stops and client sees reset. They provided trace id: trace-cc-88721 and partial tcpdump showing RST from remote IP.
Maya (Support Eng): Typical suspects: middlebox idle timeout, proxy buffering, ALB/NGINX misconfigured to buffer or close inactive sockets, or firewall doing DPI and resetting long-lived TLS tunnels.
Dan (Eng): Agreed. Ask them to check for: - Layer7 reverse proxies (NGINX/Envoy) with proxy_buffering or idle timeouts - AWS ALB idle timeout (default 60s) - Corporate middlebox TCP idle close (often 30-60s for websockets) - Any TLS/TCP proxies doing TLS terminate + re-establish with short timeouts.
Alice (SRE): Quick things to ask customer to try: 1) run wscat to stream small pings: `wscat -c "wss://private.example-corp.com/stream?model=x"` and keep sending `"ping"` every 15s to see if keepalive prevents cutoff. 2) Capture `tcpdump -i any -w ws.pcap 'tcp port 443 and host <redwood-host>'` around a failure so we can see who RSTs.
Ben (Support): They attached a small pcap excerpt: shows TLS application data then after ~47s an ACK then a RST from ip 10.7.128.1 (their NAT device). They confirmed corporate network team uses a Palo Alto box and an F5.
Maya (Support Eng): That matches an idle timeout / connection tracking issue on the middlebox. For Palo Alto and F5 you often need to enable websocket-friendly settings or increase TCP timeout. Suggested customer action: bump keepalive interval on the client and enable transparent ping frames. Also ask infra to allow egress to our endpoint IPs/ports without DPI/PTP interrupt.
Dan (Eng): For nginx/edge proxies we usually recommend these settings for proxying websockets: ```proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade"; proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 120s; proxy_send_timeout 120s;``` Also ensure `keepalive_timeout` isn't too low on upstream.
Alice (SRE): Another useful check: confirm no TLS inspection appliance is doing renegotiation. TLS renegotiation often causes a short downtime where middleboxes drop the flow. If they have TLS inspection, ask them to exempt the Redwood host from interception.
Ben (Support): I asked customer to: 1) run wscat with a 15s heartbeat 2) grab full pcap 3) share nginx/envoy/f5/paloalto timeout configs 4) add temporary egress rule to bypass TLS inspection for our host.
Customer (quoted by Ben): "We tried 15s pings, still saw disconnects but pcap shows RST from our NAT after ~46s. We'll try to bump NAT conntrack timeout and test"
Maya (Support Eng): If they can bump the conntrack to >120s and re-test that should confirm. If that fixes it, we should document an official KB: "Websocket streaming fails behind middleboxes" with checklist (ping/keepalive, proxy settings, ALB timeouts, conntrack, TLS inspection).
Dan (Eng): If they can't change infra, as a mitigation we can implement server-side application-level pings every 20s on streaming responses (we already support ping frames but some clients/proxies drop them). Also consider breaking large streams into shorter chunks with resumable tokens — but that's more intrusive.
Alice (SRE): For our internal escalation: we'll need the pcap + TLS ClientHello SNI + trace id. Assign to eng-runtime to look for server-side evidence of keepalive/ping frames.
infra-bot: New ticket created: #INC-2026-7781 assigned to eng-runtime.
Ben (Support): Customer sent updated results: after increasing NAT timeout to 180s, streaming appears stable for 5+ minutes. They will leave change for a day and confirm.
Maya (Support Eng): Good signal this was corporate conntrack/middlebox. Next steps: 1) Create KB with exact nginx/f5/paloalto snippets + keepalive guidance 2) Add troubleshooting checklist to support runbook 3) Offer to do a joint debug session with the customer's network team (we can request temporary pcap capture).
Dan (Eng): I'll draft the runtime note about adding defensive server pings and include a flag customers can opt into when behind aggressive middleboxes.
Alice (SRE): Thanks team. Ben, tag me in the final confirmation thread when customer closes the loop and we can publish KB. :thumbsup:
